4377-mrs-wiggs-of-the-cabbage-patch.title: Mrs. Wiggs Of The Cabbage Patch
4377-mrs-wiggs-of-the-cabbage-patch.creator: Unknown
4377-mrs-wiggs-of-the-cabbage-patch.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. The Wiggses lived in the Cabbage Patch. It was not a real cabbage patch, but a queer neighborhood, where ramshackle cottages played hop-scotch over the railroad tracks. There were no streets, so when a new house was built the owner faced it any way his fancy prompted.

arxiv-2102-03665.title: A symplectic formula of generalized Casson invariants
arxiv-2102-03665.creator: Shaoyun Bai
arxiv-2102-03665.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Shaoyun Bai. Suppose Y Y is an integer homology 3-sphere, Taubes [ 28 ] proved that the number of irreducible critical orbits of the perturbed Chern-Simons functional on Y Y , counted with signs, is equal to the algebraic intersection number of two character varieties associated with Heegaard splittings when the structure group is SU ⁡ ( 2 ) \SU(2) . Taubes’ result established a relationship between gauge theory and the Casson invariant.

arxiv-2205-00545.title: A sensitive search for water masers associated with star formation regions in the Local Group galaxy NGC 6822 DOI: 10.1017/pas.2026.xxx
arxiv-2205-00545.creator: C. J. P. Flanagan 1, S. P. Ellingsen 1, A. A. Cole 1
arxiv-2205-00545.description: Abstract We report the results of a sensitive search for water maser emission in the Local Group Galaxy NGC 6822 with the Karl G. Jansky Very Large Array. The observations provide tentative single-epoch detections of four candidates, associated with two infrared-bright star formation regions (Hubble I/III and Hubble IV).

arxiv-2208-03097.title: An ASP Framework for Efficient Urban Traffic Optimization Thanks: The author is a PhD Student at the Italian National PhD Programme in Artificial Intelligence https://www.phd-ai.it/ Affiliation: DIBRIS, Università degli Studi di Genova Genova, Italy
arxiv-2208-03097.creator: Matteo Cardellini
arxiv-2208-03097.description: Abstract Avoiding congestion and controlling traffic in urban scenarios is becoming nowadays of paramount importance due to the rapid growth of our cities’ population and vehicles. The effective control of urban traffic as a means to mitigate congestion can be beneficial in an economic, environmental and health way.

arxiv-2303-16219.title: Saturn’s Seismic Rotation Revisited
arxiv-2303-16219.creator: Christopher R. Mankovich, Janosz W. Dewberry, Jim Fuller
arxiv-2303-16219.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Christopher R. Mankovich, Janosz W. Dewberry, Jim Fuller. Normal mode seismology is a promising means of measuring rotation in gas giant interiors, and ring seismology presents a singular opportunity to do so at Saturn. We calculate Saturn’s normal modes of oscillation and zonal gravity field, using nonperturbative methods for normal modes in the rigidly rotating approximation, and perturbative methods for the shifts that Saturn’s deep winds induce in the mode frequencies and zonal gravity harmonics.

arxiv-2305-18574.title: On the number of primitive and quasi-primitive irreducible characters in finite groups
arxiv-2305-18574.creator: RIAD YOUMBAI, GANG CHEN
arxiv-2305-18574.description: Abstract . In this short note, it is proved that both the number of primitive characters and the number of quasi-primitive characters in a finite group G G is divisible by | G : G ′ | |G:G^{\prime}| , where G ′ G^{\prime} is the derived subgroup of G G . 1991 Mathematics Subject Classification 20D45 1.

arxiv-2310-14415.title: A New Discriminant for the Hardy Z-Function and the Corrected Gram’s law
arxiv-2310-14415.creator: Yochay Jerby
arxiv-2310-14415.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Yochay Jerby. In this paper, we introduce a novel variational framework rooted in algebraic geometry for the analysis of the Hardy Z Z -function. Our primary contribution lies in the definition and exploration of Δ n ​ ( a ¯ ) \Delta_{n}(\overline{a}) , a newly devised discriminant that measures the realness of consecutive zeros of Z ⁡ ( t ) Z(t) .

arxiv-2402-03310.title: V-IRL : Grounding Virtual Intelligence in Real Life
arxiv-2402-03310.creator: Jihan Yang, Runyu Ding, Ellis Brown, Xiaojuan Qi, Saining Xie
arxiv-2402-03310.description: Abstract There is a sensory gulf between the Earth that humans inhabit and the digital realms in which modern AI agents are created. To develop AI agents that can sense, think, and act as flexibly as humans in real-world settings, it is imperative to bridge the realism gap between the digital and physical worlds.

arxiv-2508-13367.title: Fiber bundle model of thermally activated creep failure
arxiv-2508-13367.creator: Stefan Hiemer, Paolo Moretti, Stefano Zapperi, Michael Zaiser
arxiv-2508-13367.description: Abstract An equal load sharing fiber bundle model for thermally activated breakdown is developed using transition state theory to describe the rate of elementary failures. The lifetime distribution, average, variance and their asymptotic limits for uniform fiber failure thresholds are derived and found to be in excellent agreement with simulations.

arxiv-2509-21644.title: Neutron Skin from Conserved Charge Measurements at Collider Experiments
arxiv-2509-21644.creator: Grégoire Pihan, Akihiko Monnai, Björn Schenke, Chun Shen
arxiv-2509-21644.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Grégoire Pihan, Akihiko Monnai, Björn Schenke, Chun Shen. We propose a novel method for measuring the neutron skin of heavy nuclei using collider experiments. Specifically, we demonstrate that the neutron skin thickness of the lead nucleus can be extracted in p p + 208 Pb collisions by analyzing a double ratio: The ratio of net electric charge to net baryon number measured near the lead-going rapidity, taken for high-multiplicity events and divided by the same ratio for low-multiplicity events.

arxiv-2601-07665.title: Learning to accelerate Krasnosel’skii–Mann fixed-point iterations with guarantees footnoteinfo This work was supported by Digital Futures and the Wallenberg AI, Autonomous Systems and Software Program (WASP) funded by the Knut and Alice Wallenberg Foundation.
arxiv-2601-07665.creator: Andrea Martin, Giuseppe Belgioioso
arxiv-2601-07665.description: Abstract We introduce a principled learning to optimize (L2O) framework for solving fixed-point problems involving general nonexpansive mappings. Our idea is to deliberately inject summable perturbations into a standard Krasnosel’skii–Mann iteration to improve its average-case performance over a specific distribution of problems while retaining its convergence guarantees.

arxiv-2602-23475.title: Walking with Robots: Video Analysis of Human-Robot Interactions in Transit Spaces Conference: Proceedings of the 2026 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems; April 13–17, 2026; Barcelona, Spain Proceedings of the 2026 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI ’26), Apri
arxiv-2602-23475.creator: Barry Brown, Hannah Pelikan, Mathias Broth
arxiv-2602-23475.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Barry Brown, Hannah Pelikan, Mathias Broth. The proliferation of robots in public spaces necessitates a deeper understanding of how these robots can interact with those they share the space with. In this paper, we present findings from video analysis of publicly deployed cleaning robots in a transit space—a major commercial airport, using their navigational “troubles” as a tool to document what robots currently lack in interactional competence.
